headline: Two crude bombs hurled outside PM’s Office in Dhaka
summary: One bomb exploded while the other was defused by the bomb disposal unit after two suspects on a motorcycle fled the scene.
details: Two crude bombs were thrown outside the Prime Minister's Office in Dhaka's Tejgaon area during a late-night incident on Saturday.
According to Ibne Mizan, deputy commissioner of police for the Tejgaon Division, two people on a motorcycle arrived at the scene around 1:30 am.
The suspects waited for a few minutes and looked around before hurling the explosives and fleeing towards Mirpur Road via Agargaon.
One of the bombs exploded, while the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's bomb disposal unit rushed to the scene and defused the second unexploded bomb.
Police are currently collecting CCTV footage from nearby cameras to identify and track down the suspects involved in the attack.
caption:
Two crude bombs were hurled outside the Prime Minister's Office in Dhaka late Saturday night.

Two crude bombs were thrown outside the Prime Minister's Office in Dhaka's Tejgaon area during a late-night incident on Saturday.

According to Ibne Mizan, deputy commissioner of police for the Tejgaon Division, two people on a motorcycle arrived at the scene around 1:30 am.

The suspects waited for a few minutes and looked around before hurling the explosives and fleeing towards Mirpur Road via Agargaon.

One of the bombs exploded, while the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's bomb disposal unit rushed to the scene and defused the second unexploded bomb.

Police are currently collecting CCTV footage from nearby cameras to identify and track down the suspects involved in the attack.

headline_marked: Mamata, Kejriwal and Vijayan [[detained in New Delhi]] amid protests
headline: Mamata, Kejriwal and Vijayan detained in New Delhi amid protests
summary: Opposition leaders demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities and 'vote theft'.
details: Indian opposition leaders Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal, and Pinarayi Vijayan were detained by police in New Delhi on Saturday during protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The leaders, including the Trinamool Congress chief and former chief ministers of Delhi and Kerala, were detained as they attempted to join a demonstration near Jantar Mantar.
Mamata Banerjee was detained along with five party MPs, including Derek O'Brien, after staging a sit-in at a bus stop. She was seen wearing a band-aid over her mouth during the demonstration.
Arvind Kejriwal was detained as he attempted to leave his residence, which had been surrounded by police since the morning.
Pinarayi Vijayan and CPI(M) MP John Brittas were taken to a detention centre at Chhatrasal Stadium.
The protest was organized by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led movement alleging irregularities in voter registration and electoral rolls.
The INDIA bloc has described the situation as 'vote theft' and announced plans to approach the Supreme Court on Monday to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice Surya Kant.
Further protests are scheduled for Monday to continue the fight against alleged electoral malpractice.
caption:
Three former chief ministers and multiple opposition leaders were detained in New Delhi as protests erupt over alleged 'vote theft'.

Indian opposition leaders Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal, and Pinarayi Vijayan were detained by police in New Delhi on Saturday during protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The leaders, including the Trinamool Congress chief and former chief ministers of Delhi and Kerala, were detained as they attempted to join a demonstration near Jantar Mantar.

Mamata Banerjee was detained along with five party MPs, including Derek O'Brien, after staging a sit-in at a bus stop. She was seen wearing a band-aid over her mouth during the demonstration.

Arvind Kejriwal was detained as he attempted to leave his residence, which had been surrounded by police since the morning.

Pinarayi Vijayan and CPI(M) MP John Brittas were taken to a detention centre at Chhatrasal Stadium.

The protest was organized by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led movement alleging irregularities in voter registration and electoral rolls.

The INDIA bloc has described the situation as 'vote theft' and announced plans to approach the Supreme Court on Monday to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice Surya Kant.

Further protests are scheduled for Monday to continue the fight against alleged electoral malpractice.
